subject: URGENT: Silverpine production latency & errors after model v2.1-Q4 upgrade
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@silverpine.health>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: ops@silverpine.health
Date: 2027-02-10T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Production latency spike after model upgrade - urgent

Hi Priyom,

We pushed the model update you coordinated (rwd-gpt-v2.1 + quant profile Q4) to production at 03:45 UTC and immediately saw a sharp degradation. P99 latency jumped from ~220ms to ~1.1s, throughput dropped ~40%, and our error rate (5xx) increased from 0.2% to ~2.6%. This is impacting checkout flows and real-time recommendations — our ops team is throttling traffic to keep things alive.

I've attached a small sample of logs and a CSV snapshot from our monitoring window. Can Redwood rollback that model or switch the quant profile back to Q2 immediately? We need an exec-level contact — our VP of Product is on the line.

Attachments: silverpine_latency_snapshot.csv, prod_logs_excerpt.txt

Thanks,
Alex Mercer
Sr. Engineering Manager — Platform
Silverpine Health

Subject: Re: Production latency spike after model upgrade - urgent

Summary from infra telemetry (30s buckets):
- Canary rollout: 65% of traffic to rwd-gpt-v2.1-Q4 (as Alex suggested).
- P99 token latency increase coincides with increased KV cache miss rate for long-context requests (>1024).
- Micro-profile: Q4 quantization increases GEMM kernel execution time on our A100 pools (~+240ms per token under high seq).
- Error spikes are downstream OOMs on a subset of pods using the Q4 path (we're seeing elevated retry counts).

Immediate mitigation options:
A) Immediate rollback: revert routing to previous model (rwd-gpt-v2.0-Q2) across prod. Fastest recovery, low risk to correctness.
B) Canary rollback: shift 50% -> 0% over 10 minutes to validate. Slower but less disruptive if false positive.
C) Force Q2 quant profile on existing v2.1 instances (requires a restart and warm cache, ~15-20m).

I recommend option B followed by A if metrics don't normalize in 10 minutes. I'm attaching a brief rollback_plan.pdf with play steps. Monica: can SRE execute B now?

Datadog: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/silverpine-prod/latency-overview

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

— Priyom
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: alex.mercer@silverpine.health
Date: 2027-02-10T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike after model upgrade - urgent — rollback status

Update: executed canary rollback (65% -> 25% -> 0% over ~12 minutes) starting at 09:08 PST. Metrics after rollback:
- P99 latency back to ~240ms (down ~78% from peak).
- Throughput restored to within 95% of baseline.
- Error rate returned to ~0.3% and retry churn normalized.

Root cause hypothesis: the Q4 quant profile changed kernel tiling and increased memory churn on high-seq requests, exposing cache miss/OOM across our A100 shapes. Action items:
- Temporary: keep v2.0-Q2 as prod default while we validate v2.1 with Q2 profile.
- Follow-up: infra/R&D to run a targeted perf sweep (long-context, Q2 vs Q4) and produce a regression report within 48 hours.
- CS: Marissa to confirm exec brief time and Silverpine goodwill credit.

Closing note: logs and the rollback playbook are in the incident folder (see Drive link). I'll schedule the deeper postmortem once we have the perf sweep results.

— Jonas
